title: A Dual-Agent Scheduler for Distributed Deep Learning Jobs on Public Cloud via Reinforcement Learning

problem.claim: Scheduling distributed deep learning jobs on public-cloud GPU clusters aims to reduce training fees and completion time while saving provider power costs, but the problem is NP-hard.

gap.claim: Existing approaches commonly separate ordering and placement, while learning-based methods often fail to coordinate these policies and rarely account for unbalanced machine performance and resource contention.

contributions.claim: A dual-agent scheduler jointly learns job-ordering and GPU-placement policies with multi-agent reinforcement learning.
An ordering agent uses a scalable squeeze-and-communicate strategy to improve cooperation between scheduling policies.
A placement agent uses a Random Walk Gaussian Process to learn GPU-machine performance similarities while accounting for uncertain performance fluctuation.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper explicitly presents a dual-agent scheduler and describes the Random Walk Gaussian Process for placement as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on a real-world production-cluster trace reportedly demonstrate the superiority of the model.

narrative_sequence.summary: Public-cloud GPU clusters are emerging platforms for distributed deep learning training, making scheduling important for cost, completion time, and provider power use.
The scheduling problem is NP-hard, and existing decompositions and learning-based methods leave policy cooperation and performance uncertainty insufficiently addressed.
The paper introduces a dual-agent framework with specialized ordering and placement strategies, jointly optimized through multi-agent reinforcement learning.
The authors report superiority in experiments using a real-world production-cluster trace.

source_observation.claim: Scheduling policies for coupled sub-tasks may need to be learned jointly when decisions in one sub-task affect the other.

interpretation.claim: Decomposing a hard optimization problem can preserve avoidable coordination costs if the sub-policies are optimized independently.

application.claim: For systems with interacting ordering and placement decisions, consider coordinated multi-agent or joint policy optimization.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that joint learning is preferable for all scheduling settings or workloads.

source_observation.claim: Machine-performance imbalance and resource contention create overhead and uncertainty in job duration.

interpretation.claim: Schedulers may benefit from modeling both similarity and uncertainty in resource performance rather than relying on static or uniform assumptions.

application.claim: In variable public-cloud environments, incorporate uncertainty-aware performance modeling into placement decisions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which uncertainty conditions, cluster scales, or workload types are required for this approach to help.

unknowns: No quantitative results, baselines, datasets beyond a production-cluster trace, or experimental settings are provided.
The abstract does not specify the reinforcement-learning state, action, reward, training procedure, or deployment overhead.
The abstract does not establish independent verification, generalization beyond the reported trace, or reproducibility.
